purpose: Prototype v6l: four counts that tell apart readings of v6k's results, asked for by the pre-review of outline v8 for the Journal of Writing Research (round 2) and decided by the researcher (decision 9 of .steering/20261108-paper-a-jowr-reframe; decisions 1-2 of .steering/20261108-v6l-reliability-and-r-split). (a1) The split-half reliability of each summary's features over persons, by permutation-based splits (Parsons, Kruijt & Fox 2019), so that a share below 0.60 against the person's own two parts can be read as a summary that keeps little of the operation or as a summary whose parts differ by noise. (a2) The positive control R split into its location part (R_loc: the four medians, their difference and the share of long time at sentence and subsentence starts) and its order part (R_lag: the lag-1 correlation of ln gaps), with v6k's rule cells read again under each as the gate: did R see the operations through where the gaps fall or only through their order (point of Codex in round 2)? (b1) The mean length of the P-bursts bounded by long gaps at both ends (B_complete), since odd/even parts cut 44-92% of bursts at their edges. (b2) The writer's threshold fitted after cutting inactive periods at the start and the end of the record, in the manner of the KLiCKe paper, reported beside v6k's writer and writer_fixed (appendix C).
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-11-08 after seeing v6k's record and notes (results/prototype_v6k/), and the pre-review of outline v8 (round 2). No value of R_loc, R_lag, B_complete, a split-half reliability or a trimmed writer's threshold has been computed for any person of any dataset. The persons are v6k's (decision 1): what is counted here is not new evidence on new persons but a description of v6k's cells. A first draft was sent to Codex (codex-consult, the conditions text and v6k's aggregate results only, no data; .steering/20261108-v6l-reliability-and-r-split/codex-consult-output.md) and changed after its seven points (decision 3 of that folder): the gates' cells are classed as location only, order only, both, composite only or not seen; the reliability's reading is weakened and the parts' systematic differences are added; the random parts' order and runs are fixed; the trim's boundaries are fixed and its EM keys are v6k's, so that an untrimmed record gives v6k's threshold; selections and missing values are reported; the correlation's undefined cases are fixed.
status: Description (status d) throughout: v6k's persons, whose v6k values have been seen. The reading rules below are fixed before any value of the new quantities is seen, so that the description cannot be shaped by them; they are not a confirmation.

sources.parsons_2019: Parsons, Kruijt & Fox (2019), Psychological science needs a standard practice of reporting the reliability of cognitive-behavioral measurements, Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science 2(4) (the preprint text read for round 1 of the pre-review, sources/parsons2019.txt), verbatim: 'This process involves a large number of repeated calculations in which the data is randomly split into two halves and the reliability estimate is calculated'; the Spearman-Brown correction rs = 2r / (1 + r) 'where rs Spearman-Brown corrected estimate, and r is the observed Pearson correlation between the two halves'; the report 'averaging the results of 5000 random splits'; 'the lower and upper 95% percentile intervals for both the splithalf and the Spearman-Brown corrected estimate'; 'we recommend 5000 as the minimum'; odd/even estimates 'have the potential to vary greatly depending on which trials happen to be odd and even'.
sources.klicke_inactive: Tian, Crossley & Van Waes (2025), the KLiCKe corpus (the PDF of v6k's sources), p. 42-43, verbatim: 'we first removed the inactive periods at the beginning (e.g., reading instructions, pre-planning) and the end of the processes (e.g., proof-reading, waiting for submission) to delimit the analyses to the actual text production'; no length is given. p. 30-31: the task page 'issued warnings whenever the writer was detected to be inactive for more than 2 minutes'.

data: as v6k (files and SHA-256 in v6k's and v6e's conditions).

participants.persons: v6k's: KUPA from position 437 of v6's draw order, the first 200 eligible under v6b's rule; LWP from position 204 of v6e's, the first 200 eligible under v6e's rule (v6k's draw, reused). The run checks that the SHA-256 of each sorted id list equals v6k's record, and that positions 0-436 (KUPA) and 0-203 (LWP) give v6's, v6b's and v6e's persons as in v6k.
participants.count_1_persons: v6k's count 1 persons per dataset and task (KUPA essay 178, KUPA copy 200, LWP 197 in v6k's record; checked).

units_rows_parts: as v6k: sentences (counting 'before' unless a row says otherwise), the rows of v6k (text/after, text/none, inside/before, shuffled/before, shuffled_in_halves/before, random_half) with v6k's operations and keys, parts odd/even and halves.

stages.reused: S0, S1, U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I, R and Bsd_complete@2000 exactly as v6k (v6k's code, imported).
stages.R_loc: the first six numbers of R (median ln gap at sentence, subsentence, word and within-word starts; sentence minus within; the share of long time at sentence and subsentence starts at 2 s). A person has R_loc exactly when they have R.
stages.R_lag: the seventh number of R (lag-1 correlation of ln gaps over pairs of consecutive gaps both held by the part; 0 with fewer than 3 pairs or a constant side, as v6b). 1 number.
stages.B_complete: at 2 s: the mean length (presses) of the part's P-bursts bounded by long gaps at both ends (the bursts that Bsd_complete uses); a part with no such burst has no value. 1 number. No identity by construction is claimed for it (it depends on where the first and last long gap of each run fall). It selects bursts: reported per set and baseline over the text's parts, the five-number summaries of the number of complete bursts and of their share of the part's bursts and presses; per cell the persons left out for want of a complete burst.
stages.U_B_Bsd_at_trimmed_thresholds: U, B and Bsd (v6k's definitions) at the trimmed writer's thresholds (thresholds below), on the same sentences and parts as v6k: the trim changes only the gaps the mixture is fitted on, not the parts summarised.

thresholds.fixed: 2000 ms only (index 0, as v6k). 1000 ms and 500 ms are v6k's.

trim.rule: for a record (press times t_0 < ... < t_N, gap g_i = t_i - t_(i-1), i = 1..N, N >= 1) and a length T; a gap is long here if g_i >= T - 1e-6 ms (v6's tolerance, at every step). Start: let the window be the first min(10, M) gaps of the remaining record (M its number of gaps). If the window holds a long gap, let j be the last one, drop every press before the press that ends it, and the gaps up to and including it; repeat until the window holds none. End, on what remains: the window is its last min(10, M) gaps; if it holds a long gap, let j be the first one, drop the press that ends it and every press after, and the gaps from it on; repeat. If at any step fewer than 11 presses remain, the record is 'consumed': no trimmed threshold (counted). A record that drops nothing is 'untrimmed' (its trimmed record is the record itself). Equal press times do not occur (v6.clean drops them). The trim is a set of kept gap indices [a, b) of the record; the labels stay with their gaps. Reported per set: the numbers of records trimmed at the start, at the end, untrimmed and consumed; the five-number summaries of the steps repeated at each end, the presses dropped and the dropped share of the record's total time.
trim.lengths: T = 120 s (main: the inactivity length of KLiCKe's task page) and T = 30 s (sensitivity), decision 2.
trim.fit: v6k's mixture (fit_writer: the same starts, floors, discards and BIC rule) fitted to ln of the 'word' gaps (v6b.labels) in [a, b), with v6k's keys unchanged (the same row index): an untrimmed record gives exactly v6k's theta_w, so a difference between theta_t and theta_w comes from the gaps dropped, not from the random starts. theta_t = exp(mu_j + 3 sigma_j) as v6k. A trimmed record with fewer than 2 'word' gaps has no theta_t (counted).
trim.use: two forms per T, as v6k's writer and writer_fixed: trimT (refitted: every operated series is trimmed by the same rule on its own times and fitted on its own; text/after and text/none reuse the text's fit) and trimT_fixed (the text's trimmed theta_t kept for every operated series). Index in keys: trim120 5, trim120_fixed 6, trim30 7, trim30_fixed 8. A record without theta_t is left out at that threshold (counted per cell). Not done (limits): a form that keeps the text's [a, b) for the operated series.
trim.reported: per dataset and task over count persons: the trim tallies above; five-number summaries of theta_t, of the weight of component j, of the gaps fitted and the frequencies of k; on the persons with both, the five-number summary of ln theta_t(text) - ln theta_w(text) (theta_w: v6k's untrimmed text fit, refitted here with v6k's code and keys) and the number of persons whose difference is exactly 0; per operated row the five-number summary of |ln theta_t(row) - ln theta_t(text)|. Baaijen's example value (1,686 ms, between-word pauses as the sum of the intervals before and after the space, on linear transitions) is named beside, not compared as a target.

count_1.how: v6k's count 1 (v6b.one) per dataset, task, baseline, row and stage on all persons with a vector (gate 0), for R_loc, R_lag, B_complete@2000 and U, B, Bsd at trim120, trim120_fixed, trim30 and trim30_fixed; and for S0, S1, I, R and U, B, Bsd, Bsd_complete at 2000 again (the reuse check).
count_1.rule_persons: for each of v6k's rule stages (U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I) and beside the rule (Bsd_complete@2000, B_complete@2000): on the persons with the stage and R (v6k's rule persons; R_loc and R_lag exist exactly when R does), the stage, R, R_loc and R_lag, in the 12 main cells (KUPA essay and LWP; odd/even and halves; inside/before, shuffled/before, shuffled_in_halves/before).
count_1.keys: v6k's key1: numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 90, dataset, task, stage, row index, baseline, threshold, gate]) with v6k's stage, row, baseline and threshold indices, and the new stages R_loc 8, R_lag 9, B_complete 10 and thresholds as above. The gate of the rule persons is 1 + the stage index of the rule stage (v6k's), the same for its R, R_loc and R_lag (B_complete's 1 + 10). So v6k's cells are reproduced exactly with v6k's keys.

reliability.what: per dataset and task, on the count 1 persons, of the text (text/before, counting 'before'): for each feature of S0 (7), U@2000 (4), B@2000 (1), Bsd@2000 (1), B_complete@2000 (1), Bsd_complete@2000 (1), I (3) and R (7: R_loc's six and R_lag), the split-half reliability over persons.
reliability.splits: 5000 random splits (Parsons' minimum). In split s, a person's n sentences are permuted by numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 93, dataset, task, place]) (one generator per person, drawing its permutations in the order s = 0..4999); the first floor(n / 2) of the permutation form part A, the rest part B. Each part's sentences are then taken in their original order, and the part's vectors are v6k's part vectors of those sentences: its held gaps in index order, runs of consecutive gap indices of the original record (two sentences join a run only if they are adjacent in the record and both in the part), lag-1 pairs only within the part's held gaps (v6b), no gap or pair across a sentence of the other part. Random splits cut more runs than halves do; halves (a block split) is reported beside.
reliability.estimate: for a feature in split s: on the persons with a vector for the stage in both parts in that split (at least 10, else no value), r_s = the Pearson correlation over persons of the feature in A and in B; rSB_s = 2 r_s / (1 + r_s), undefined for r_s = -1. A split where the feature is constant on one side over those persons, or r_s = -1, has no value (counted by reason); a non-finite feature value stops the run. Negative r_s are kept (rSB_s is then negative). Reported per feature: the mean of r_s and of rSB_s over splits with a value, their 2.5% and 97.5% percentiles over those splits (Parsons' 95% percentile interval, not a confidence interval for the persons), the number of splits with a value and without (by reason), the minimum, median and maximum number of persons per split; for the fixed parts odd/even and halves (one split each) the same r and rSB, and beside them the mean and the median absolute difference A - B over persons and the standard deviation over persons of A and of B (a systematic difference between the parts lowers no correlation but widens the baseline).
reliability.reading: descriptive, no threshold used as a rule. A feature's mean rSB below 0.50 is named 'low'. A low reliability means that the parts' values of a feature do not order persons alike; it can come from noise within persons or from small differences between persons, and it is not a measure of count 1's baseline (a Euclidean distance over scaled features within a person). It is reported beside the count 1 cells of its stage as one reason a baseline can be wide, not as the reason.

rule.part_1_again: v6k's rule (12 main cells, the six labels, the cells fixed by construction, at least 4 evaluable cells) applied three times to the same rule persons' counts: gate R (v6k's; must give v6k's labels and classes exactly), gate R_loc and gate R_lag (the stage is evaluable in a cell only if the gate reads it above 0.60). Reported per stage and gate: the label and the classes by dataset and row; and per main cell (on each rule stage's persons): the classes of R, R_loc and R_lag, and the cell's kind among 'location only' (R_loc above, R_lag not), 'order only' (R_lag above, R_loc not), 'both', and, where R is above and neither part is, 'composite only'; 'not seen' where R is not above.
rule.reading_of_the_gates: fixed before running. A cell where R_loc reads above 0.60 is one where the location part of the reference, on those persons and with its features and scaling, shows the operation beyond the smallest difference; a stage that does not read the cell then shows the operation less than that part does, by this distance and baseline (not 'keeps less of where the gaps fall' in general: dimension, scaling and overlap of features differ). A cell of kind 'order only' or 'composite only' is one where v6k's gate did not rest on the location part; v6k's readings of those cells are reported as such. A cell of kind 'order only' does not show that the operation left the location unchanged. A label that changes between gate R and gate R_loc is reported as changed, with the cells that changed it.
rule.B_complete: beside the rule, no label: its class in the 12 main cells under gate R and under gate R_loc, and the edge share of v6k's B beside it.
rule.part_2_trim: descriptive, as v6k's part 2: for U, B and Bsd in the 12 main cells (gate 0 counts), the class at trim120, trim120_fixed, trim30 and trim30_fixed and the number of cells whose class equals that at 2 s (a cell agrees only if both are counts).

checks.reuse: before any new quantity is reported, and stopping the run otherwise: the persons' id SHA-256 equal v6k's; v6k's count 1 persons per set; for every main cell and every rule stage and Bsd_complete@2000, the rule persons' counts of the stage and of R equal v6k's record (persons, share_vs_own and its interval); gate R reproduces v6k's part 1 labels; gate 0 counts of S0, S1, I, R, U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000 and Bsd_complete@2000 in every row and baseline equal v6k's record; the untrimmed text fit's five-number summary of theta_w equals v6k's theta_w_text per set. These are aggregates over persons; a mismatch of persons or values shows in them, and the per-person values are not written.
checks.parts: the reliability's part vectors for the fixed parts odd/even and halves equal v6k's part vectors for every person and stage (the code of the splits is the code of count 1).
checks.construction: v6k's per-person identities at 2000, and B's identity (G + r) / (L + r) and the multiset identities of B and U (stages.by_construction of v6k) at trim120_fixed and trim30_fixed, where the threshold is the text's (a violation stops the run). R_loc and R_lag are R's numbers (checked equal per person).

prediction: Claude's, written before running. P1: R_loc reads shuffled/before and shuffled_in_halves/before above 0.60 in all 8 of their main cells (rule persons of U@2000). P2: R_lag reads them above 0.60 in at least 6 of the 8. P3: under gate R_loc the labels of U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000 and I equal v6k's. P4: in KUPA essay, every S0 feature has mean rSB at least 0.80. P5: in KUPA essay and LWP, each of U@2000's four features has mean rSB at least 0.50. P6: B_complete@2000 reads no shuffle cell above 0.60 (gate R, rule persons). P7: the median of ln theta_t(text) - ln theta_w(text) at T = 120 s is within 0.1 of 0 in every set (few records hold a gap of 2 min in their first or last 10 gaps). P8: at T = 30 s the median theta_t over text records is below v6k's median theta_w and above 2000 ms in every set. No value of v6l had been seen.
main_cells: fixed before running, shown first: the rule again under gates R, R_loc and R_lag (labels, and the per-cell location/order table); the reliability of U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I, R and S0 (mean rSB and percentile interval per feature) in KUPA essay and LWP; B_complete in the 12 main cells; the trimmed thresholds (per set: records trimmed, theta_t against theta_w); then the rest in the order of this file.

record.public: results/prototype_v6l/record.json: counts and summaries over persons and the provenance; no press time, gap, key, text, per-person vector, per-person value, per-person threshold, per-person reliability input or id (ids only as the SHA-256 of their sorted list). The data are not redistributed.
record.provenance: git commit and dirty state of the conditions, code and lock; SHA-256 of the conditions, the earlier conditions and records, the code and the data; versions.

limits_written_before: The persons are v6k's, whose v6k values were seen before this file: nothing here is a confirmation. The split-half reliability is of single features over persons; count 1 compares a Euclidean distance over scaled features within a person, so a low reliability is a reason for a wide baseline, not its measure. The random splits mix sentences from anywhere in the session, unlike odd/even and halves, so a split's parts are closer in phase than halves. R_loc and R_lag are parts of one composite chosen on earlier persons; R_loc's share of long time depends on 2 s. The trim is a rule written here for press times; KLiCKe's trim was made on Inputlog's .idfx with no stated length, so the trimmed threshold is a version of the preprocessing, not KLiCKe's. The time before the first press and after the last is already outside the records. Baaijen's pauses were between-word intervals as the sum before and after the space, on linear transitions; here 'word' gaps are those before the first letter after a space, revisions are not removed, and the trim is the only preprocessing added. Many correlated cells; agreements are not independent replications. The trim is applied to an operated series on its own times (trimT), so at trimT the operation, the gaps kept and the fit change together; trimT_fixed isolates the threshold of the text.
rerun_rule: as v6k: if a defect of the code is found after the first run, the first record is kept unchanged, the fix and the reason are committed, and the rerun is reported separately beside the first.
generator: as v6k (checked by v6k's code against v6k's conditions).
